summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old man with a history of coronary artery disease, diabetes, hypertension, and prior pulmonary embolism on warfarin presented with pleuritic chest pain, cough, and shortness of breath. He was subtherapeutic on admission with an INR of 1.4. A CT angiogram showed minimal partially occlusive filling defects consistent with resolving pulmonary emboli and no acute clot. Cardiac enzymes were negative, and the pain was attributed to pleural irritation from healing clots. He was started on a heparin drip and transitioned to enoxaparin for bridging while adjusting warfarin. His chronic conditions remained stable, and he was discharged home with instructions to continue anticoagulation, monitor for worsening symptoms, and obtain an INR check in clinic.
